# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable and widely supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI, git, and certificates in a single layer
# - build-essential: Provides C/C++ compilers and make
# - cmake: Build system generator required by Kripke
# - git: For cloning the source repository
# - ca-certificates: For secure network communications (e.g., git clone)
# - openmpi-bin & libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI implementation for parallel execution
# After installation, clean up apt cache to reduce image size
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone, build, and install Kripke from the master branch in a single RUN command
# This minimizes layer count and cleans up build artifacts.
# 1. Clone the master branch of the Kripke repository and its submodules (CORRECTION: added --recurse-submodules)
# 2. Create a build directory and enter it
# 3. Configure the build with CMake for a Release build with MPI enabled
# 4. Compile the source code using all available processor cores
# 5. Copy the final executable to a system PATH location (/usr/local/bin)
# 6. Clean up the source code directory to keep the final image small
RUN git clone --branch master --recurse-submodules --depth 1 https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /kripke && \
    cd /kripke && \
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    cmake .. -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DENABLE_MPI=ON && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke.exe && \
    cd / && rm -rf /kripke

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments
# These settings are crucial for running MPI jobs in Docker/Kubernetes
# - Allow running as root, which is common in containers
# - Exclude loopback and docker network interfaces to prevent MPI from using them for inter-process communication
# - Disable shared memory mechanism that can be problematic in some container runtimes
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_exclude=lo,docker0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_exclude=lo,docker0

# Set the working directory
WORKDIR /

# Set a default command to run when the container starts
# This will display the application's help message. The user will typically
# override this with `mpirun` to execute a parallel job.
CMD ["kripke.exe", "--help"]

  namespace: default

  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.

kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 to run on a single node.

  # The total number of MPI tasks, matching the process grid (4*4*3).
  tasks: 48

  # Keep pods and resources after the job finishes for debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Enable strict validation of the MiniCluster spec.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod spec modifications to target specific hardware.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

  flux:
    container: {}

  # Define the application container to be run by the Flux Operator.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      runFlux: true
      launcher: false
      # FIX: Changed --zones from 52,52,52 to 60,60,60 to fix the assertion failure.

      # 60 is divisible by both 4 (for X/Y) and 3 (for Z), unlike the previous value of 52.
      command: /usr/local/bin/kripke.exe --procs 4,4,3 --niter 20 --layout ZGD --zones 60,60,60
